label: Atalante Migliorotti
summary: Florentine musician and maker of string instruments, named by the Anonimo Gaddiano as Leonardo's companion on his journey to Milan.

value.text: Sent to Milan with Leonardo with a lyre for Ludovico, c.1482

claims.statement: The Anonimo Gaddiano says Lorenzo de' Medici sent Leonardo, with Atalante Migliorotti, to the Duke of Milan to present a lyre. This is what the text says; no contemporary record confirms it.

value.text: 'Una testa ritratta d'Atalante che alzava il volto'

claims.statement: A list of works in Leonardo's hand in the Codex Atlanticus (c.1482) is said to include a portrait head of Atalante raising his face. Not confirmed in this round.

value.text: Orfeo at Mantua 1491; lirone for Isabella d'Este 1505; works at St Peter's 1513

claims.statement: Reported to have sung Poliziano's Orfeo at Mantua in 1491, to have made a lira for Isabella d'Este in 1505, and to have supervised works at St Peter's in Rome from 1513.
